q: The 'Global Trade Alert' and the 'Trade Policy Review' are:
options: WTO mechanisms for transparency and surveillance of trade policies
programmes of the UNIDO for industrial development
tools of the World Bank for project appraisal
initiatives of the IMF for debt sustainability
explanation: The Trade Policy Review Mechanism and the Global Trade Alert are part of the WTO's transparency and surveillance architecture, and they examine the trade policies of members and the measures that may distort trade.

q: The 'General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade' of 1947 is significant because:
options: it created the International Monetary Fund
it was the first multilateral agreement on tariffs and provided the institutional base for the WTO
it was the first treaty to liberalise services trade
it established the Bretton Woods exchange rate system
explanation: The GATT of 1947 set out the principles of trade policy, including most favoured nation treatment, and after eight rounds of negotiations it was replaced by the WTO Agreement in 1995.

q: The 'General Agreement on Trade in Services' of the WTO applies to:
options: trade in services such as tourism, transport, financial and business services
only the supply of services in the agriculture sector
the tariff preferences of developing countries
the settlement of disputes relating to services
explanation: GATS was the first multilateral agreement to liberalise and rules-basedly discipline trade in services, and it has annexes on specific sectors such as financial services, telecommunications and movement of natural persons.

q: The 'Trade Facilitation Agreement' of the WTO aims to:
options: provide for the abolition of all customs duties
reduce the tariffs on agricultural products
simplify customs procedures and reduce the cost of border compliance for traders
subsidise the agricultural exports of developing countries
explanation: The Trade Facilitation Agreement, in force since 2017, simplifies and harmonises customs procedures, sets a time limit for the release of cargo and requires advance rulings and risk management, with a special and differential treatment for developing countries.

q: India's export of business process services is facilitated by the:
options: the restriction of work-from-home arrangements for exporters
the imposition of a high export duty on software
the absence of any special economic zones for the IT sector
IT parks and the SEZ policy, with a large share of the workforce trained at the university and technical institute level
explanation: The policy of setting up software technology parks and SEZs for the IT sector, together with the strength of engineering education, created the skilled labour pool that made India a global outsourcing destination.

q: For Indian exports, the recognition of the 'BIS' certification:
options: helps exporters meet the quality and labelling requirements of the destination country
entitles them to a rebate on customs duty
is mandatory only for imports
replaces the need for a certificate of origin
explanation: BIS certification, and the Quality Control Orders, enable Indian exporters to demonstrate conformity with international standards and thereby access markets with strict technical regulations.

q: The 'Foreign Trade Policy' of India is:
options: a part of the Income Tax Act
an annual statement of the RBI
the tariff schedule notified by the Department of Revenue
a document of the DGFT that outlines the policy framework for exports and imports
explanation: The Foreign Trade Policy is notified by the DGFT under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, and it is supplemented by the annual tariff notifications of the Department of Revenue.

q: The Indian postal network enables exports by:
options: issuing letters of credit for exporters
facilitating exports of small value consignments through the international mail and the e-commerce export hubs
certifying the quality of exported goods
operating the customs bonded warehouses
explanation: The Department of Posts runs e-commerce export hubs and an export mail scheme that allows small traders and exporters to ship consignments abroad through the international mail network.

q: India's coastal shipping policy aims to:
options: increase the number of inland waterways in the Ganga basin
ban the movement of cargo by road
shift a greater share of the freight from road and rail to waterways to reduce logistics cost and congestion
privatise all the major ports without any regulation
explanation: India's coastal shipping and inland waterways policy seeks to move cargo from road and rail to cheaper and more environment friendly waterways, and the National Inland Waterways Act, 2016 designated three national waterways.

q: India joined the 'Belt and Road Initiative' in:
options: 2022, at the SCO summit in Samarkand
2019, at the Second Belt and Road Forum in Beijing
2013, at the launch of the initiative in Beijing
2016, at the G20 summit in Hangzhou
explanation: India formally joined the Belt and Road Initiative in 2019 at the Second Belt and Road Forum in Beijing, on the condition that the forum respect India's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

q: The ASEAN-India Dialogue Relations were upgraded to a summit in:
options: 2014, at the ASEAN-India Summit in Nay Pyi Taw
1997, at the ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur
2008, at the ASEAN-India Summit in New Delhi
2020, at the ASEAN-India Summit in Hanoi
explanation: The ASEAN-India Dialogue Relations were elevated to the level of a summit in 2014 in Nay Pyi Taw, and the ASEAN-India Centenary was observed in 2022 marking fifty years of dialogue relations.

q: The voting power of a country in the IMF is determined by:
options: the number of its diplomats in the capital
its population
its quota, which also determines its share of the credit line and of the distribution of SDRs
its contribution to the World Bank alone
explanation: A country's quota in the Fund determines its voting power, its access to the credit line and its share of the allocation of SDRs, and the quota is reviewed every five years through the general review and the fourteen-yearly quota increase.

q: Under the Minimum Reserve System, the RBI is required to:
options: maintain a minimum cash balance with the scheduled commercial banks
maintain a minimum reserve of gold with the public
keep the exchange rate of the rupee fixed
hold a minimum stock of foreign assets against the import demand of the economy
explanation: Under the Minimum Reserve System, adopted in 1957, the central bank holds a minimum stock of foreign assets sufficient to cover a certain period of imports, and the RBI's stock of foreign exchange is part of these reserves.

q: Under FEMA, a Non-Resident Indian is a person who:
options: require NRIs to convert all foreign currency into rupees on arrival
permit NRIs to hold Indian currency only in national banks
prohibit NRIs from holding any foreign currency
allow NRIs to hold foreign currency and Indian currency in designated accounts without restrictions on the former
explanation: NRIs may hold foreign currency in foreign currency accounts and freely use it, though they cannot hold foreign currency in the form of Indian bank notes, and Indian currency holding by NRIs is subject to specified limits.

q: The 'merchandise exports' of India consist mainly of:
options: iron ore and coal alone
engineering goods, petroleum products, gems and jewellery, pharmaceuticals and chemicals
only agricultural products
mainly services and tourism receipts
explanation: Merchandise exports are dominated by engineering goods, refined petroleum products, gems and jewellery, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and cotton textiles, while services make up a separate and growing share of total exports.

q: Inward remittances in India are a significant contributor to:
options: the current account balance and the consumption expenditure of migrant households
the capital expenditure of the states
the primary deficit
the fiscal deficit of the central government
explanation: Remittances support household consumption and smooth the current account, and their distribution across states is uneven, with the largest shares going to the poorer states of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.

q: The key labour market indicator that captures the share of the working-age population engaged in gainful activity is the:
options: unemployment rate
dependency ratio
labour force participation rate
population density
explanation: The labour force participation rate is the share of the working-age population in the labour force, and a low female participation rate is a persistent feature of the Indian labour market.
